question: The value of a machine depreciates at the rate of 10% per annum. If its present value is ₹1,62,000, then what was the value of the machine 2 years ago?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of **depreciation** = 10% = 1/10.

Value ratio for 1 year = 10 : 9.

Value ratio for **2 years** = 10² : 9² = 100 : 81.

Given, 81 units = ₹1,62,000 → 1 unit = ₹2,000.

Original value (100 units) = 100 × ₹2,000 = ₹2,00,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present Value (Vₚ) = ₹1,62,000

Rate of depreciation (r) = 10%

Time period (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Vₚ = V₀ × (1 − r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9d36e79ff58433d6fbf55623a8ae4e0c6acdffd9f1305d3496ca571f7115c16.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1,62,000 = V₀ × (1 − 10/100)²

⇒ 1,62,000 = V₀ × (90/100)²

⇒ 1,62,000 = V₀ × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ 1,62,000 = V₀ × (81/100)

⇒ V₀ = (1,62,000 × 100) ÷ 81

⇒ V₀ = 2,000 × 100

⇒ V₀ = 2,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Depreciation Formula

It is similar to Compound Interest but with a negative rate: Amount = Principal × (1 − R/100)T.

Appreciation

If the value increases, the formula becomes: Future Value = Present Value × (1 + R/100)T.

Successive Percentage Change

For two years of depreciation, the effective rate is −a − b + (ab/100). For 10% p.a., effective change = −10 − 10 + 1 = −19%.
